narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **19% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that the school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning light on a dashboard—it’s not saying you’ll fail, but it’s telling you to pay attention and take action before things get worse.

The biggest reason behind this recommendation is **how you chose this school**. Most students pick their school because of the courses offered or because it’s close to home, but you chose it for its reputation. While reputation can be a good thing, it might mean you’re not as engaged with the school’s day-to-day environment, which can make it harder to stay on track. The model also noticed that you haven’t had any past class failures, which is actually a positive sign—it suggests you’re capable of doing the work, but you might need extra support to stay focused.

Another key factor is your **aspirations for the future**. Unlike most students, who are all aiming for higher education, your goal is already set. While this is great motivation, it might also mean you’re under extra pressure to perform well, which can sometimes lead to stress or distraction if you’re not careful.

Finally, the model picked up on your **study habits**. You’re studying between 2 to 5 hours a week, which is less than many of your peers who are studying 5 to 10 hours. While you’re not completely behind, this is an area where small improvements could make a big difference.

The good news is that remedial courses are designed to help you fill any gaps and get back on track. To make the most of them, try to balance your study time, stay engaged with your school’s community, and use the extra support available to you. You’ve got this!
